correctness.rationale: The first nonconstant term of a rational quotient at infinity cannot be unimodular on any non-affine real polynomial graph: its leading real-part coefficient either survives or cancels, in which case its first displacement by the common real coordinate survives and dominates later Laurent terms. The complex quotient of the polynomial restriction algebra is exactly C[U,V]/(U-V-2iP((U+V)/2)); separate-degree multiplicativity gives kernel square dimension. Hermitian polarization, generic evaluation determinants, and the rank-two compactness argument complete all statements. The included checker exactly tested 45 rank instances and four sample matrices; none of these finite tests is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The rational-level intersection theorem permits exceptional rational compositions but does not rule out all rational unimodular functions on our graph. Generic/unrestricted complex-plane evaluation schemes in the 2019 paper do not imply the sharp fixed-curve Hilbert profile formula.

value.rationale: A natural design class—all polynomial graphs—is characterized completely by the affine/non-affine boundary. Exact intensity-profile rank holds simultaneously at every curve degree m and signal degree d, with a sharp phase transition at m=d+1 between Hermitian lifting and phase-only reconstruction. Generic interpolation works in any arbitrarily small real interval; this exact geometric Hilbert-function fact is useful for deterministic curve-constrained phaseless measurement design, not a minor numerical variant.
